overall_summary: Deduplicated performance analysis shows that space and 'What If' planetary scenario hooks published within the last 7 days are dominating both views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes/comments-per-view). Specifically, hypothetical space immersion titles (e.g., falling into extreme planets) generate the highest velocity and engagement. Content older than 7 days experiences a sharp drop-off in daily views, emphasizing the need for continuous fresh uploads in high-performing categories.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Space Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) achieved over 970 to 1,024 views rapidly with high like-to-view ratios (up to 38 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If' immersive space and planetary survival scenarios featuring extreme physical conditions.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing bizarre planetary environments like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) consistently pull over 700 to 1,000 views within days of release.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing short-form content highlighting visually striking, bizarre exoplanets or cosmic anomalies with strong hook adjectives.

weak_patterns.evidence: Older psychology and memory trivia clips (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', views dipping to single/double digits) show extremely low retention and long-tail discovery velocity compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic psychological trivia unless tied to a high-concept sci-fi or thriller narrative framework.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic animal facts (e.g., 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts', 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever') generated minimal comments and lower view velocity outside of specific outlier spikes.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal-related storytelling toward cinematic survival or extreme 'what if' scenarios rather than static listicle facts.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Coldest Known Place in the Universe (The Boomerang Nebula)?
next_video.opening_direction: Immediately plunge the viewer into a conceptual 1-second drop into a freezing cosmic void colder than deep space itself.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the gas expanding so fast it creates temperatures colder than the cosmic microwave background would instantly freeze your breath into glittering crystal dust.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'What If You Fell Into...' format combined with extreme thermodynamic anomalies, which dominate current 7-day view velocity and engagement metrics.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not use previously covered planets (TrES-2b, diamond planets, burning ice planet)
Must feature a completely new celestial body (Boomerang Nebula)
Must maintain high visual descriptive pacing suitable for AI micro-drama/cinematic space rendering

experiment: Test whether framing a space phenomenon purely as an extreme physical survival sensation ('What If You Fell Into...') outperforms declarative declarative fact statements ('The Star Colder Than Ice') by at least 25% in the first 48 hours.
